content: Hypertriglyceridemia, or elevated triglyceride levels, can arise from a variety of underlying causes. These include genetic predispositions, familial factors, metabolic disorders, and the use of certain medications. Life-threatening causes are defined as conditions that, if left untreated, may lead to death or irreversible disability within 24 hours. However, hypertriglyceridemia itself does not fall into the category of life-threatening conditions. Common causes of hypertriglyceridemia include diabetes mellitus and obesity. When categorizing causes by organ systems or in alphabetical order, it is important to consider the broader diagnostic framework. The 2018 American Heart Association (AHA) and American College of Cardiology (ACC) guidelines on the management of blood cholesterol provide a comprehensive approach to understanding and addressing hypertriglyceridemia.
